title: Adobe Premiere Pro sequence contracts
body:
# Adobe Premiere Pro sequence contracts

This is an **experimental integration, with no installed Premiere native acceptance recorded**. The bundled UXP panel implements a bounded read-only `sequenceContract` using public Adobe APIs. Linux runs fail explicitly with `NATIVE_ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE`; host planning, schema inspection and verification of retained responses work without Adobe imports. Node tests execute the actual companion with contract doubles and are host-only evidence.

Declare the exact absolute saved project path, active sequence name, width/height, integer fps and ordered source ranges. See `examples/schemaxis/premiere-sequence.json`. Windows drive paths and macOS absolute paths are accepted as native identities; the host does not read the source files. Each clip uses zero-based `startFrame` and positive `frameCount`; the native out point is expected to be exclusive. Ranges accumulate from timeline zero. Rates 24/25/30/50/60 use 254016000000 ticks per second, serialized as exact decimal strings. No JavaScript floating-point tick arithmetic or BigInt is required. At most 128 clips and 600 timeline frames are accepted.

The native sequence must have exactly one unmuted video track, no captions or transitions, and at most 8 empty audio tracks. Disabled, adjustment, reversed, offline, nested, merged, multicam or proxy clips are rejected. Source identity, native in/out/duration/start/end ticks, sequence dimensions/timebase/end and runtime identity must match. This checks structure; it does not inspect source bytes, effects, intermediate time remapping, colour, pixel fidelity, audio output or rendered media. Equal endpoint durations do not prove unchanged playback inside a clip.

The companion reads the complete bounded observation twice and rechecks active project/sequence GUIDs around each read. Matching observations detect observed changes; they are not an atomic snapshot. Keep Premiere idle during inspection. The panel never selects, edits, saves, imports, renders or exports a project.

## Native setup and execution

1. Use Windows or macOS with Premiere 26.5.0 or later and Adobe UXP Developer Tool 2.2 or later. Enable developer mode. Load `src/schemaxis/adaptors/premiere/uxp/manifest.json` using UDT. Its manifest 5 host is `premierepro`, with only `localFileSystem: request` permission. There is no network, external-process, arbitrary-JavaScript or unrestricted filesystem permission.
2. Open the saved native project and activate the declared sequence. Create a private local bridge directory. Replace project/source identities in your authored JSON with exact native paths.
3. Run `schemaxis run your-contract.json --output-directory /absolute/new-attempt --premiere-bridge /absolute/private-jobs --timeout 300`. The dedicated CLI option configures transport; `configure premiere` configures executables and is not a bridge configuration command. A private config may instead set `locations.premiereBridge` to the existing absolute directory.
4. While the host waits, inspect `/absolute/new-attempt/bridge-job.json`. Open the Schemaxis Sequence Contract panel, click its button and select that exact fresh `jobDirectory` using the native folder picker. The panel reads `request.json`, observes the active sequence and writes the response. Select the job subdirectory, rather than its parent bridge directory.
5. Run `schemaxis verify /absolute/new-attempt` to repeat offline checks. Read `observation.json`, `verification.json`, the retained request/response and failed result if applicable. Artifact 0 is a JSON `sequenceObservation`; no project or video artifact is produced.

Each attempt creates an unpredictable per-attempt directory (mode 0700 where supported, otherwise inheriting the private bridge folder access controls) and fresh 128-bit nonce. Request bytes, response filename and returned requestSHA256 must agree; stale previous responses cannot satisfy a new attempt. The panel checks bounded expiry and re-reads the request before writing and publishing. It writes a pending file fully, then publishes with documented UXP `Entry.moveTo`, so the host reads the completed response name. The host rejects symlink/nonregular/oversized response files before parsing, bounds JSON to 1 MiB, and checks the shared elapsed deadline/cancellation before success. No native application subprocess is owned or killed. Cancellation ends the host wait; expired/cancelled responses cannot become accepted output. Failed bridge jobs are retained for diagnosis; use a fresh attempt rather than overwriting them.

Ordinary retained-byte or authored-plan changes fail verification. A request hash and native identity fields do not provide remote attestation or defend against someone fabricating all local evidence. Trust the supplied panel and local filesystem. Host-side expressions, document references and finite analytic planning use the shared runtime; every native visit still needs a fresh human-selected UXP job. No workflow scheduling, automatic reuse or shared native-inspection workspace hook is advertised for this human-mediated transport.

## Qualification recipe

On a native machine, independently prepare and inspect a silent six-frame `colours.mp4` source (H.264 AVC, 25 fps; red, green, blue, yellow, cyan, magenta in order) and two 32x24/25 fps sequences in a saved project. `Schemaxis Colours` contains source frames 3..5 followed by 0..1. `Schemaxis Repeat` contains frames 1..2 twice. Use one video track and empty audio tracks, without transitions/effects/retiming. Verify this manually in Premiere before running the tool.

Run `python tools/qualify_premiere.py --bridge /absolute/private-jobs --project-path /absolute/colours.prproj --source-path /absolute/colours.mp4 --output-directory /absolute/new-acceptance`. For each printed case, activate its sequence and select the fresh printed job folder in the panel. The tool checks literal expected ticks/ranges and rejected mutations independently. It retains actual responses and a report. This recipe is currently unexecuted on installed Premiere; `absorbedVersion` remains null and no native qualification receipt is registered. The ordinary conformance kit also contains baseline and held-out cases; its unattended timeout/cancel expectations are not yet native-qualified for a human-mediated panel.

## Primary references

- [Premiere UXP APIs](https://developer.adobe.com/premiere-pro/uxp/resources/fundamentals/apis/), [Sequence](https://developer.adobe.com/premiere-pro/uxp/ppro-reference/classes/sequence), [VideoClipTrackItem](https://developer.adobe.com/premiere-pro/uxp/ppro-reference/classes/videocliptrackitem), [TickTime](https://developer.adobe.com/premiere-pro/uxp/ppro-reference/classes/ticktime), [Guid](https://developer.adobe.com/premiere-pro/uxp/ppro-reference/classes/guid).
- [Host information](https://developer.adobe.com/premiere-pro/uxp/resources/recipes/host-info/), [manifest](https://developer.adobe.com/premiere-pro/uxp/plugins/concepts/manifest/), [filesystem recipe](https://developer.adobe.com/premiere-pro/uxp/resources/recipes/filesystem-operations/), [UXP Entry.moveTo](https://developer.adobe.com/photoshop/uxp/2022/uxp-api/reference-js/modules/uxp/persistent-file-storage/storage).

The MP4 example uses an Adobe-listed import format; it is human-prepared and independently inspected. It does not imply that the Shotcut Matroska/FFV1 fixture imports into Premiere. See [Adobe supported file formats](https://helpx.adobe.com/premiere/desktop/organize-media/import-files/supported-file-formats.html).
